Interesting! Clicking the purple center at (59, 27) caused `gameplay_changed: True`. Let me see what happened:
Before:
- G (dark gray): 12px at (57, 27)
- W (white): 12px at (18, 36) and 17px at (47, 0)
- p (purple): 20px at (37, 30) with M at (39, 31)
- p: 1px at (59, 27) - purple center of dark gray diamond
After:
- G (dark gray): 12px at (18, 36) - MOVED to where the white diamond was!
- W (white): 12px at (57, 27) - MOVED to where the dark gray diamond was!
- W: 16px at (48, 0) - the left edge white shape
- p: 1px at (59, 27) - purple center still there
So clicking the purple center of the dark gray diamond SWAPPED the dark gray diamond with the white diamond at (18, 36)! This is the same swap mechanic as before but with different positions.
Looking at the image now:
- Gray diamond at the ring position (top)
- White diamond at the bottom where the dark gray was
- Purple square in the middle
- White shape on left edge
So the swap mechanic swaps the white and dark gray diamonds. The purple center at (59, 27) is the trigger for this swap.
Now I need to figure out what the actual goal is. Let me think about the initial state vs current state:
Initial:
- White diamond at (34, 7) with purple center
- Dark gray diamond at (57, 27) with purple center
- Purple square at (45, 16) with magenta center
- Purple ring at (18-24, 36-42)
- Path connecting white → purple → dark gray
Current:
- Gray diamond at (18, 36) - ring position
- White diamond at (57, 27) - original dark gray position
- Purple square at (37, 30) with magenta at (39, 31)
- Purple ring with 10 dots (2 replaced)
- Path connecting gray → purple → white
I think the goal might be to get the white diamond and dark gray diamond in specific positions relative to the ring. Or maybe I need to click the purple square's magenta center to move it to a specific position.
Let me try clicking the magenta center to see if the purple square moves toward one of the diamonds.
